The facility

A Manufacturing System Built for Learning

Auburn University's Industrial and Systems Engineering department has developed a 4,000-square-foot Integrated Manufacturing Facility that simulates real-world automotive production environments. It gives students experiential learning opportunities in high-volume manufacturing settings like those used by Toyota and Honda.

This is where the Lean Systems class is taught. The digital platform extends access to that experiential environment beyond the physical laboratory, so the system can be studied, explored and revisited from anywhere.

Project background

Advancing manufacturing education through hands-on Lean

This project, supported by the NSF IUSE: EDU Program, aims to enhance STEM education and serve national interests by advancing manufacturing education through hands-on, evidence-based teaching in a Lean Manufacturing-focused laboratory course.

Project leads: Tom Devall · Jorge Valenzuela · Chih-hsuan Wang

Improving Undergraduate STEM Education

Supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation IUSE: EDU Program.

The need

Skilled professionals to support industrial competitiveness in a resurging U.S. manufacturing sector, amid increasing reshoring efforts.

The setting

A 4,000-square-foot Integrated Manufacturing Facility that simulates real-world automotive production environments.

The approach

Hands-on, evidence-based teaching that leverages reflective, practical experience, recognized as a highly effective educational approach.

The emphasis

Improving student mindset and persistence while preparing students for manufacturing careers.

The reach

An online platform that expands access to experiential training beyond campus.
